methods.label: Substitute and simplify
methods.explanation:
To find \(f(x+h)\), replace every \(x\) in the formula by \(x+h\). When subtracting \(f(x)\), the constant terms cancel, while the linear terms contribute \(-2h\). Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(x+h)-f(x)
&=5\bigl((x+h)^2-x^2\bigr)-2h\\
&=5(2xh+h^2)-2h\\
&=10xh+5h^2-2h\\
&=\boxed{h(10x+5h-2)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The second line uses \((x+h)^2=x^2+2xh+h^2\). This identity holds for all real \(x,h\), including \(h=0\). The answer is \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
